extracted.intended_audience: game writers, narrative designers, hiring managers, and aspiring game writers in the game industry
extracted.subtask_description: High-level professional guidance describing what game writing is, the kinds of tasks game writers perform, the value of craft/process, and community resources for practitioners and those who work with them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of game writing tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: "Game writers include those in the game industry who write dialogue scripts, construct overarching narrative structure, produce documentation and articles, and a myriad of other writing tasks.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates the types of writing work expected of game writers (dialogue scripts, narrative structure, documentation, articles). Use this as a non-exhaustive checklist of domains game writing can cover when defining roles or evaluating whether a candidate/employee’s responsibilities match the position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role identification and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: "Sometimes, they are specifically identified as writers, and other times they find themselves picking up writing duties as an addition to their primary jobs.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals that game writing roles frequently overlap with other disciplines; evaluate practitioners for both dedicated writing experience and the ability to perform writing alongside other responsibilities (e.g., design, production). Hiring and assessment should account for multi-role contexts and informal route into writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of craft and process
rubrics_metrics.description: "The craft and process of game writing, and the quality that good game writing brings to game development as a whole, have been undervalued for too long.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes assessing and prioritizing writing craft and process in development teams. Use this as guidance to advocate for appropriate resourcing, recognition, and integration of writers into game development workflows; consider quality of narrative integration and writing process maturity when evaluating projects or teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community membership and professional connection as a resource
rubrics_metrics.description: "Our membership includes writers, narrative designers, those who hire and work with writers and narrative designers, and those who want to be writers and/or narrative designers. Our website can be found at game-writing.com. Additionally, we have a Discord server and a mailing list to keep in touch with each other.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat membership, community channels, and listed resources as part of professional development and evaluation: participation indicates engagement with best practices, networking, and ongoing learning. Use these resources for mentorship, hiring outreach, and role development.
